correctness.rationale: On the orthogonal complement of the constants, the objective is N times the trace of the inverse Laplacian. Its second directional derivative is strictly positive for any nonzero Laplacian perturbation, and the edge-to-Laplacian map is injective here. As a connected allocation approaches disconnection the smallest restricted eigenvalue goes to zero. Compactness therefore gives an attained unique optimum, fixed by S_p × S_q; either orbit weight zero would isolate original vertices. Homogeneity forces full spending. In an orthonormal left-standard block the diagonal is (qx,x+y) and the off-diagonal is −√q x, giving determinant qxy; the right block gives pxy. In the constant block the three principal two-minors are pqxy, qxy, pxy, so their sum is Nxy. The remaining (p−1)(q−1) directions have eigenvalue x+y. Summing inverse eigenvalues verifies all coefficients. The full-budget t parametrization is regular and bijective on the positive budget segment, so strict convexity on the segment justifies uniqueness of the stationary root, without claiming convexity in t. In the balanced case c_m/a_m ∼ m; for Q>P the root is bounded above by √(P/Q), hence tends to zero and gives m t² → P/(Q−P). Swapping sides and equality handle the other prices. In the fixed-δ window the limiting derivative equation has a unique sign-changing zero because φ(t)=(1−t)(1+t)^3/t² strictly decreases from +∞ to −∞. Uniform convergence on compact positive t-intervals brackets the finite-size root at that zero. These are general proof checks; verify.py was inspected, not run. Its spectral and optimizer examples are finite numerical corroboration, not certificates of the limits.

value.rationale: The natural design problem reveals support retention despite an asymptotically vanishing expensive allocation. The weighted trace resolves the competition between the leading (x+y) term and the spoke-specific singular terms, quantifies the exact optimum for finite graphs, and yields a continuous positive crossover distinct from matching deletion on ordinary bicliques. That makes the result useful beyond a unit-weight numerical evaluation.
